title: First Missing Positive: Every Key in Its Own Locker
summary: Use the array as its own lookup table: swap each value into slot value − 1, then the first wrong slot names the gap.

analogy.scenario: Three lockers, numbered 1 to 3, hold keys tagged 4, 1, and 2. Each key belongs in the locker with its number. Which is the smallest locker number whose key is missing?

mapping.real: Moving a key to its own locker
The first locker without its key

takeaway.pattern: Cyclic sort (the array as a hash table)
takeaway.summary: Value v belongs in slot v − 1. Swap each in-range value into its slot, ignoring values out of range; then the first slot i not holding i + 1 means i + 1 is missing, else n + 1.
takeaway.timeComplexity: O(n): each swap puts one value in its final slot
whenToUse: Values 1…n that index into the array itself
Missing or duplicate numbers with O(1) extra space

scenes.narration: Three lockers, numbered 1 to 3, hold keys tagged 4, 1, and 2. Each key belongs in the locker with its number. What's the smallest number whose key is missing?
scenes.caption: Lockers 1–3 hold keys tagged 4, 1, and 2: which key is missing?

scenes.narration: Searching every locker for key 1, then key 2, and so on is a nested loop. A separate lookup table needs extra space. Instead, the lockers are the lookup table: put each key in its own locker.
scenes.caption: Searching for 1, then 2, then 3 is a nested loop

scenes.narration: Locker 1 holds key 4, but there's no locker 4, so it can't be put anywhere. Leave it for now.
scenes.caption: Key 4 has no locker here: leave it

scenes.narration: Locker 2 holds key 1. Swap it into locker 1, where it belongs; key 4 comes back to locker 2.
scenes.caption: Key 1 swaps into locker 1

scenes.narration: Key 4 still can't move. Locker 3 holds key 2: swap it into locker 2, and key 4 ends up in locker 3.
scenes.caption: Key 2 swaps into locker 2

scenes.narration: Now check the lockers in order. Lockers 1 and 2 hold their own keys, but locker 3 holds key 4. So 3 is the first missing key.
scenes.caption: Locker 3 holds key 4, not 3: key 3 is missing

scenes.narration: Lockers are array slots: value v lives at slot v minus 1. Each swap places one value for good, so it's O(n) time with no extra space.
scenes.caption: Lockers are slots; the array is its own lookup table
